page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.mn4.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance belonging to the ecs.mn4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 32 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation and 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics are generally limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression falling into the weak or poor categories. Conversely, multi-core performance is more robust, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains consistently average across both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks, though the overall PassMark memory score is weak. The hardware supports AVX and AVX-512 instruction sets, which assist in vector calculations, but lacks newer extensions like AMX or AVX-512 VNNI.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the contrast between weak single-core and average multi-core capabilities, the ecs.mn4.8xlarge is suited for workloads that can distribute tasks across its 32 cores. Appropriate use cases include multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and database operations, which all achieved average benchmark marks. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks for smaller models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model and lack of bundled local storage position this instance as a resource-dense option for non-latency-critical, parallelizable workloads where dedicated CPU performance is not strictly required.
